scope: Cases where materially or linguistically differentiated documentary version states are later grouped together by archival transfer or custody.
central_claim: Custody can recombine version states that research practice had differentiated, so present or historical container relations must be analysed separately from version relations.

research_states.state: compact neat table; current link to 1864 large bundle not directly stated

events.manifest_description: in Khas and in English, Statement of the Revenue of the Province of Jumla
events.source: William Wilson Hunter, Life of Brian Houghton Hodgson (1896), Appendix B reproducing the August 1864 India Office presentation list
events.interpretation: At least Khas and English version states of the Jumla revenue family were intentionally co-custodied in one large transfer bundle after documentary differentiation.
source_control: The manifest establishes large-bundle co-custody, not exact lesser-wrapper or sheet adjacency.
The Farsi derivative is part of the modern source family but is not explicitly named in the 1864 manifest line.
Modern volume separation must not be projected backward as the 1864 arrangement.

next_actions: Locate original 1864 India Office accession/packing list if surviving.
Map the sixth large bundle to modern Mss Eur Hodgson volume/item identities.
Determine whether Khas and English Jumla states were in separate lesser wrappers inside the large bundle.
Check whether other 1864 manifest entries deliberately co-group originals and English translations in the same bundle.
